transcript.text: Thank you, Mara. I'm ready to give my formal recorded readout on the privacy and clinical regulatory aspects of the proposed joint research agreement. My formal recorded readout is as follows: First, regarding the publication provisions — the current draft permits publication of project results without adequate restrictions. Based on my review and confirmation with the product lead and privacy office, the company's non-negotiable clinical-data position requires two amendments: one, publication containing patient-level data must be expressly prohibited; two, de-identification must be required before any permitted external publication. These restrictions must be incorporated into the publication clause before the agreement can be approved. Second, regarding data processing and regulatory compliance — the agreement involves diagnostic software development, which may implicate clinical regulatory requirements depending on the intended use and data sources involved. The university partner must be required to comply with all applicable privacy and clinical regulations in connection with any patient data accessed or processed under the project. Third, regarding data ownership and use — any clinical or patient data generated during the project must remain subject to the company's privacy and data governance policies, and the university's use of such data must be limited to the research scope defined in the agreement. In summary, my formal recorded readout identifies one critical required revision — the publication provisions must be amended to prohibit patient-level data publication and require de-identification — and two additional compliance conditions regarding regulatory compliance and data governance. That concludes my formal recorded readout. It is complete.

transcript.text: Thank you, Mara. Here is my formal recorded IP readout on the intellectual property aspects of the proposed joint research agreement. My formal recorded readout is as follows: First, regarding background technology — my review of the university's master research agreement and the controlling schedule supplied overnight confirmed that background patents U1, U2, and U3 are licensed to the company only for noncommercial academic use. The current draft grants the university an exclusive commercial license to all background technology used in the project, which would improperly include these three patents. The final agreement must exclude U1, U2, and U3 from any commercial license grant and require separate written university consent before any commercial use of those patents. This is a critical required revision. Second, regarding foreground IP — the agreement should clearly define ownership and allocation of rights to any newly developed IP arising from the project, consistent with the company's IP policy and the parties' respective contributions. Third, regarding IP infringement and warranties — the agreement should include appropriate representations regarding each party's right to grant licenses to the background technology it contributes, and standard infringement indemnification provisions should be incorporated to protect the company's interests. In summary, my formal recorded readout identifies one critical required revision — patents U1, U2, and U3 must be carved out of the commercial license grant with separate written university consent required before commercial use — and two additional IP conditions regarding foreground IP ownership and infringement protections. That concludes my formal recorded readout. It is complete.
